Largest items in the current directory

Lists the 10 largest files and directories here (dotfiles excluded).

du -hs * | sort -rh | head -10

disk, storage, du

Find files over 100 MB

Finds files over 100 MB on the root filesystem, largest first.

sudo find / -xdev -type f -size +100M -exec du -h {} + 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -20

disk, files, find

Tail systemd service logs

Follows journalctl logs for a service in real-time.

journalctl -u <service-name> -f

logs, systemd

Stop the process listening on a port

Sends SIGTERM to the process listening on a TCP port.

Caution. Use kill -9 only if the process ignores SIGTERM: -9 skips its shutdown and cleanup.

kill $(lsof -t -i:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN)

process, port, kill

Find the processes using the most CPU

Lists the top 10 processes consuming the most CPU.

ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd,%mem,%cpu --sort=-%cpu | head -11

cpu, performance, ps

Search string recursively

Searches for a string inside all files in a directory.

grep -rnw '/path/to/somewhere/' -e 'pattern'

search, grep, files

Create soft symlink

Creates a symbolic link pointing to a target file or directory.

ln -s /path/to/target /path/to/link

files, symlink, link

Set permissions on directories only

Recursively changes permissions of directories only (leaving files untouched).

find . -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \;

permissions, chmod, directories

Print specific columns with awk

Prints only the 3rd and 5th columns of a space-separated file.

awk '{print $3, $5}' data.txt

awk, text, processing

Find and replace in a file with sed

Replaces 'old-string' with 'new-string' inline in a file.

sed -i 's/old-string/new-string/g' config.yaml

GNU sed. On macOS, use sed -i '' instead of sed -i.

sed, replace, text

Delete log files older than 30 days

Finds .log files older than 30 days under /var/log and deletes them.

Caution. Deletes files permanently. Run it once without -delete to see the list first.

sudo find /var/log -type f -name "*.log" -mtime +30 -delete

find, cleanup, logs

Sync directories securely

Uses rsync to synchronize two directories over SSH, showing progress.

rsync -avz --progress /local/dir/ user@remote:/remote/dir/

rsync, sync, ssh

Check free memory

Shows total, used and available memory in human-readable units.

free -h

memory, ram

Check disk space

Shows filesystem disk space usage and types.

df -Th

disk, storage

Find and change owner

Finds files owned by root and changes them to another user.

Caution. Changes ownership of everything it matches. Check the path first; run against / it can break the system.

find /path -user root -exec chown user:group {} +

chown, permissions
